h1:
Where to Stay in Chiang Rai?
12 Hotels We Actually Reviewed
Prices Compared Across 3 Sites!
heroSub: 12 hand-picked Chiang Rai hotels across every budget — from an all-inclusive Mekong-side resort at the Golden Triangle down to in-town dorms from ฿250/night. Covering the main areas: the Golden Triangle (Chiang Saen), the Kok River and the town centre. From roughly ฿250–35,000/night.
introH2: 🏞️ Why does choosing the right area in Chiang Rai matter?
introHtml: Chiang Rai covers more ground than most people expect, and each area has a completely different vibe. The Golden Triangle–Chiang Saen sits at the far north on the Mekong, about 1.5 hours' drive from town — a zone of riverside resorts and elephant camps. The Kok River runs through town and is a calm resort-and-boutique belt that's still close to the centre. And the town centre, around the Clock Tower, Night Bazaar and Walking Street, is easy to explore on foot with hotels at every price point. Many people book without checking the area, then lose hours shuttling back and forth by road. This guide rounds up 12 Chiang Rai hotels we've already reviewed across every tier — with real guest-review scores, a 3-site price comparison and direct booking links for each.
mrtHtml: Chiang Rai has no metro. Getting around means rental car, scooter, taxi, songthaew, or Grab (limited supply). From Mae Fah Luang Airport (CEI) it's about 15 minutes into town. The Clock Tower and Night Bazaar area is walkable, but Wat Rong Khun (White Temple), Wat Rong Suea Ten (Blue Temple) and the Golden Triangle all need a car. The Golden Triangle–Chiang Saen is about 1.5 hours from town. The areas in this guide: Golden Triangle–Chiang Saen — Mekong-view resorts, elephant camps, quiet · Kok River — riverside resorts and boutiques, calm but close to town · Town Centre — Clock Tower, Night Bazaar, Walking Street, easy to explore on foot.

toc.name: Anantara Golden Triangle Elephant Camp & Resort
The Legend Chiang Rai Boutique River Resort & Spa

entries.name: Anantara Golden Triangle Elephant Camp & Resort
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Golden Triangle, Chiang Saen · on the Mekong
entries.storyHtml: The top score in this guide at 9.6 — Anantara Golden Triangle is an all-inclusive 5-star resort on the Mekong at the Golden Triangle, Chiang Saen. Its standout, found nowhere else here, is the on-site elephant camp and the close-up elephant experiences, plus the Jungle Bubble clear domes where you sleep watching elephants and stars in the jungle. The rate includes most meals, drinks and activities. Real guest reviews praise the three-country Mekong views and the attentive service, but flag the high price and the location about 1.5 hours from Chiang Rai town.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: The rate bundles meals and activities, so the per-night cost works out better than it first looks. Jungle Bubbles are limited and book out fast — reserve well ahead if you want one.
pros: Top score in the guide at 9.6 — Anantara-level service
On-site elephant camp and close-up experiences you won't find elsewhere
Jungle Bubble clear domes — sleep watching elephants and stars
Rate includes most meals, drinks and activities
cons: Highest price in the guide — best for a special trip or honeymoon
Out at Chiang Saen, about 1.5 hours from Chiang Rai town

entries.name: The Riverie by Katathani
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Kok River, central · walk to Night Bazaar
entries.storyHtml: The Riverie is a luxury 5-star resort on the Kok River in the town centre, and the most-reviewed luxury option here — 945 reviews, 9.4. The draw is a riverside setting that's quiet yet within walking distance of the Night Bazaar, plus a large river-view pool. The surprise is that entry rooms start from just ฿2,600 — excellent value for a 5-star resort of this calibre. Real guest reviews praise the value and location, though some note the building shows its age in places.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: The entry Deluxe is already good value, but step up to a Deluxe River for a direct Kok River view from the balcony. Travelling as a family? The Family Suite works out cheaper per head.
pros: Most-reviewed luxury pick here — 945 reviews, 9.4, reliable
Kok River in the centre — quiet but walk to the Night Bazaar
Large river-view pool, full resort feel
5-star luxury from just ฿2,600 — outstanding value
cons: An established resort — parts of the building show their age
River-view rooms sell out fast; book ahead to secure one

entries.name: Le Meridien Chiang Rai Resort
entries.badge: 🌊 Luxury resort on the Kok River
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Kok River, near town · 53 sqm rooms
entries.addr: 221/2 Moo 20, Kwaewai Road, Robwieng, Chiang Rai
entries.storyHtml: Le Meridien is a 5-star boutique resort in the Marriott family on the Kok River, near town, scoring 9.3 from 494 reviews. The highlights are entry rooms that run a generous 53 square metres and a riverside setting that's calm yet just a few minutes' drive from the centre. Real guest reviews praise the spacious rooms, the leafy riverside gardens and the steady Marriott service standard. A good fit if you want a riverside luxury resort that's still easy to reach town from.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: The entry Deluxe is already 53 sqm, so only step up to River View if you specifically want the Kok River view from the balcony. It's a Marriott Bonvoy property if you collect or redeem points.
pros: Marriott family, steady service standard, 9.3
Entry rooms a generous 53 sqm — bigger than many here
Kok River — calm yet a few minutes' drive into town
Leafy riverside gardens and pool, great for relaxing
cons: Riverside — not within walking distance of the Night Bazaar; a car helps
Pricier than the entry-level riverside resorts in this guide

entries.name: The Legend Chiang Rai Boutique River Resort & Spa
entries.addr: 124/15 Moo 21 Kohloy Road, Rim Kok, Chiang Rai
entries.storyHtml: The Legend is a 4-star boutique resort on the Kok River, and the most-reviewed boutique option here — over 1,442 reviews, 9.2. The standout is its distinctive Lanna architecture, spacious studio rooms with large walk-in showers, and pool villas for those who want privacy. The riverside setting is quiet and relaxing. Real guest reviews praise the beautiful design and the calm, but note you'll want a car since it isn't within walking distance of town.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: The entry Superior Studio is already spacious and attractive. Only move up to the One Bedroom Pool Villa if you're a couple or small family who wants a private pool.
pros: Most-reviewed boutique pick — 1,442 reviews, 9.2, reliable
Distinctive Lanna architecture, beautifully styled
Spacious studio rooms with large walk-in showers
Quiet Kok River setting, pool villas available
cons: Riverside — not walkable to town, a car helps
A long-running resort, some corners show their age

entries.name: Nak Nakara Hotel
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Town centre · by the Hilltribe Museum
entries.storyHtml: Nak Nakara is a 4-star boutique hotel in the town centre with Lanna-style decor, from just ฿1,500, scoring 9.3. The draw is a central location by the Hilltribe Museum, walkable to the Clock Tower and Walking Street, plus a pool — rare at this price in the centre. Real guest reviews praise the lovely Lanna styling and the easy-to-explore location. Reviews are still modest (116) but the score holds high and steady.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: The entry Boutique Double is good value if location is your priority. Travelling as a family? The Family Room sleeps 3–4 and works out cheaper per head.
pros: Lovely, distinctive Lanna styling, 9.3
Town centre — walk to the Clock Tower and Walking Street
Has a pool — rare at this price in the centre
4-star boutique from just ฿1,500 — great value
cons: Review count still modest (116) versus others here
Central location means some rooms catch street noise; ask for an interior room

entries.name: Mercy Hostel
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Town centre, near Clock Tower · small pool
entries.storyHtml: Mercy Hostel is the most-reviewed property in this guide — over 2,970 reviews, scoring a high 9.2, with dorms from just ฿250. Unlike a typical hostel, it has a small pool, a gym and a shared kitchen — at dorm prices. The location is central, near the Clock Tower and Walking Street. Real guest reviews praise the cleanliness, the better-than-the-price facilities and the friendly vibe. A great fit for backpackers and budget travellers who want more than a plain dorm.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Want quiet and a bit of privacy? Book a Studio — still cheaper than a hotel. You can use the pool and the shared kitchen to save on meals over a longer stay.
pros: Most-reviewed in the guide — 2,970 reviews, high 9.2
Small pool, gym and shared kitchen — beyond dorm prices
Dorms from just ฿250 in the town centre
Clean, friendly, near the Clock Tower and Walking Street
cons: It's a hostel — dorms mean sharing space
The few private Studios sell out fast

entries.name: Wiang Inn Hotel
entries.badge: 📍 Town centre, by the Night Bazaar
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Town centre · by the Night Bazaar
entries.storyHtml: Wiang Inn is a 4-star hotel in the town centre with a prime spot by the Night Bazaar, scoring 8.8 from 371 reviews. It's one of Chiang Rai's long-standing hotels, with a pool and full facilities, from just ฿1,400. The location is walkable to the Night Bazaar, markets and restaurants. Real guest reviews praise the location and value, but note the building and some rooms show their age — go for a renovated Deluxe.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: The Deluxe rooms are larger and feel newer than the entry Superior. The spot by the Night Bazaar makes evening eating and strolling very convenient.
pros: Town centre by the Night Bazaar — walk to food and sights
Pool and full facilities included
4-star from just ฿1,400 — good value
Great for those who prioritise a central location
cons: A long-standing hotel — building and some rooms show their age
Ask for a renovated Deluxe for a fresher room than the Superior

entries.name: Diamond Park Inn Chiangrai Resort
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Near the Clock Tower · town centre
entries.storyHtml: Diamond Park Inn is a 3-star city resort near the Clock Tower with a pool, from just ฿1,100, scoring 8.7 from 112 reviews. The draws are a central location near the Clock Tower and main sights, plus a pool and parking. Real guest reviews praise the value, clean rooms and location, but note facilities are basic as you'd expect at 3 stars. A good fit for road-trippers who want a place with a pool and easy parking.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Driving around Chiang Rai? This is handy for the parking and the Clock Tower location. The Deluxe rooms are a touch larger with garden/pool views over the entry Superior.
pros: Central location near the Clock Tower and main sights
Pool and parking, from just ฿1,100
Clean rooms, 8.7 — good value for 3-star in the centre
Handy for road-trippers who want easy parking
cons: Facilities are basic, as expected at 3 stars
Review count still modest (112) versus others here

entries.name: Pimanninn
entries.badge: 💬 Huge review count, has a pool
entries.storyHtml: Pimanninn is a budget hotel in the town centre with the largest review count in this guide — over 6,142 reviews, from just ฿750. It bills itself a "Luxury Economy Hotel", meaning a pool and gym at a budget price. The 7.9 score isn't as high as the top of the table, partly because the sheer volume of reviews surfaces both praise and complaints. Real guest reviews like the value and the pool, but note rooms and service are basic — don't expect a big-hotel experience.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If you want a cheap stay that still has a pool, this fits. Stepping up to Deluxe or Suite for a few hundred baht more gets you a larger, fresher room than the entry Standard.
pros: Largest review count in the guide — 6,142, lots of data
Pool and gym, from just ฿750
Central location, easy to get around from
Good value for budget travellers who still want a pool
cons: 7.9 isn't as high as the top picks — rooms and service are basic
High review volume surfaces both praise and complaints; keep expectations realistic

entries.name: Baan Bua Guest House
entries.badge: 🪙 Quiet guest house near the bus station
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Jetyod / old town · near the bus station
entries.storyHtml: Baan Bua is a budget guest house in the Jetyod old-town area, with rooms from just ฿400, scoring 8.3 from 258 reviews. The draw is a quiet garden setting with a homey, welcoming feel, near the bus station for easy onward travel. There are fan rooms, A/C rooms and a family room. Real guest reviews praise the cleanliness, the friendly owner and the value. A good fit for backpackers and budget travellers who want a quiet private room rather than a dorm.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: On the tightest budget, go for a fan room — but a little extra for an A/C room is far more comfortable in the hot season. Near the bus station, handy if you arrive or leave by coach.
pros: Rooms from just ฿400 — great value for a private room in town
Quiet garden setting, homey and welcoming
Near the bus station, easy onward travel
Friendly owner, clean rooms, 8.3
cons: It's a guest house — facilities are basic
The cheapest fan rooms can get warm in the hot season

entries.name: Phowadol Resort & Spa
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Near airport & Walking Street · garden cottages
entries.storyHtml: Phowadol is a 3-star garden-cottage resort near the airport and Walking Street, from just ฿900, scoring 6.9 from 43 reviews — the lowest in this guide. The draw is the leafy garden-cottage setting and a location near the airport, handy for early flights or late arrivals. Real guest reviews like the greenery and the price, but several flag that rooms and some facilities are dated and due for a refresh — which is why it lands last. A fit for those who weigh an airport-side location and price over freshness.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Choose a Superior or Deluxe Cottage — they sit in the garden and are larger than the block Superior rooms. Handy as a last-night stay before an early flight, given the airport proximity.
pros: Leafy garden-cottage setting, from just ฿900
Near the airport — handy for early flights or late arrivals
Near Walking Street for evening strolls and food
Good for those who prioritise an airport-side location and price
cons: Lowest score in the guide at 6.9 — rooms are dated, due for a refresh
Some facilities show their age; ask to see a renovated room

faqTitle: FAQ — Common traveller questions about Chiang Rai hotels

faq.q: ❓ Which area should I stay in in Chiang Rai?
faq.a: It depends on your travel style. The town centre, around the Clock Tower and Night Bazaar, is the easiest for eating and exploring on foot, with hotels at every tier (Nak Nakara, Wiang Inn, Diamond Park Inn, Mercy Hostel, Cat & Turtle, Pimanninn). The Kok River is a calm resort belt that's still close to town (The Riverie, Le Meridien, The Legend). The Golden Triangle–Chiang Saen, at the far north on the Mekong, suits a special trip (Anantara Golden Triangle).

faq.q: ❓ How much do Chiang Rai hotels cost?
faq.a: Prices vary widely: dorms and guest houses start around ฿250–650 a night; mid-range hotels and resorts up to 4-star run roughly ฿900–3,500; 5-star luxury resorts on the Kok River start around ฿2,600–9,500; and the all-inclusive resort at the Golden Triangle starts around ฿35,000 (meals and activities included). All are approximate starting rates for standard rooms.

faq.q: ❓ Where should I stay to visit the Golden Triangle?
faq.a: The Golden Triangle–Chiang Saen is about 1.5 hours by road from Chiang Rai town. If you want to stay on the Mekong with a close-up elephant experience, Anantara Golden Triangle Elephant Camp & Resort is the main choice. But if you're using Chiang Rai as a base and visiting the Golden Triangle as a day trip, staying in town or by the Kok River is more convenient and cheaper — then drive or join a tour out and back in a day.

faq.q: ❓ How far ahead should I book a Chiang Rai hotel?
faq.a: For weekdays outside the tourist season, 2–4 weeks ahead is enough. But in the cool-season high season (November–February) — a pleasant and popular time, especially around New Year and the flower festival — good rooms fill fast, so book 1–2 months ahead or more.

faq.q: ❓ How do I get around Chiang Rai — do I need to rent a car?
faq.a: Chiang Rai has no metro. Getting around means rental car, scooter, taxi, songthaew and Grab (limited supply). The town centre around the Clock Tower and Night Bazaar is walkable, but Wat Rong Khun (White Temple), Wat Rong Suea Ten (Blue Temple) and the Golden Triangle are outside town and need a car or a tour. If you plan to see several sights, renting a car or scooter is more convenient and better value.

faq.q: ❓ Which site is cheapest for booking Chiang Rai hotels?
faq.a: Prices on each site (Agoda, Booking.com, Trip.com) vary with each platform's promotions. We recommend opening all three to compare before every booking — each review page in this guide includes price-comparison links, which can save you several hundred baht a night.
